metaDescription: Baybay Sweet jackfruit is a jackfruit variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Baybay Sweet is a registered jackfruit variety, also sold or known as Baybay Sweet langka or NSIC Jf 07. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2009 as NSIC 2009 Jf 07. Gil C. Impas bred it. Its record notes a yield of 30 fruits and above.

items: **Yield:** a recorded yield of 30 fruits and above.

blocks.text: Key facts about Baybay Sweet jackfruit
When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Baybay Sweet was about 18 years old and about 12 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 30 fruits and above. It bears every year, with fruit in Aug. Sept, Jan Feb. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.
The pests and diseases that hit jackfruit fields most often: [mealybug](/pests/mealybug). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of Baybay Sweet weighs about 7966.67 grams, and its shape is ellipsoid. The flesh is golden yellow and smooth and crispy. Its sweetness measured 23.19 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 44.24 percent of the fruit. Its fruiting season is Aug. Sept, Jan Feb, bearing annual.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Harvest:** Fruits August to September and January to February.
**Fruit:** Ellipsoid, about 8 kg, yellowish green smooth skin, golden yellow, crisp, dry (not juicy) bulbs, strong aroma, about 23 Brix, about 44 percent edible.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: a Leyte farmer's jackfruit that fruits twice a year. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Baybay Sweet jackfruit

Pick a selection by flesh: firm and crisp for fresh eating and processing, or soft and sweet. Grafted trees of a named selection bear true. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Baybay Sweet langka the same as Baybay Sweet?
items.a: Yes. Baybay Sweet langka is another name for Baybay Sweet, registered as NSIC 2009 Jf 07. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows a recorded yield of 30 fruits and above. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Baybay Sweet?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
